claims.claim: Archer broadened from eVTOL air taxis toward an aerospace/defense physical-AI platform through its announced Boeing transaction and Halo/Thunder autonomous hybrid VTOL program with Anduril.
Archer reports ZEE, an aviation-focused AI foundation model, demonstrated real-time airport-surface trajectory prediction, creating a potential software/safety layer beyond aircraft manufacturing.

risks.risk: Strategic breadth increases integration and execution complexity before the core Midnight business reaches mature certification and commercial scale.

unknowns.unknown: Economic contribution and integration timing of the announced Boeing assets remain prospective.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was $5.0M while net loss was $263.2M and adjusted EBITDA was negative $177.1M; cash, equivalents and short-term investments ended at $1.561B.
Archer completed piloted city-to-city Midnight flights and said it was preparing for operations later in 2026 under the U.S. eVTOL Integration Pilot Program.

risks.risk: Cash burn remains substantial relative to nascent revenue, making certification timing, capital intensity and commercialization critical execution variables.

contradictions.contradiction: Operational/certification milestones are advancing while current revenue remains very small versus operating losses.

unknowns.unknown: Timing and economics of scaled passenger service and full FAA type certification remain uncertain.
